name: application-navigation-menu
title: Navigation Menu
description: Horizontal site navigation bar where a top-level item is either a plain link or a trigger that opens a mega-menu panel of grouped sub-links with descriptions.
useWhen: Building a top nav bar where one or more items need to reveal a panel of related sub-links, not just a flat list.
You want link descriptions visible in the dropdown, not just bare labels.
Marking the current page via aria-current for an active-state nav item.
avoidWhen: The bar represents application commands (File, Edit, Save) rather than site sections — use Menubar instead.
Navigation is a vertical sidebar rather than a horizontal bar — use Side Menu or Vertical Menu instead.
You only need a single flat row of links with no dropdown panel — plain links in a nav element are simpler.
responsiveBehavior: The bar is a centered single row; below the breakpoint where all items fit, collapse into a mobile menu trigger rather than wrapping or scrolling the bar.
accessibility: The nav element carries aria-label so it's distinguishable from other landmark regions (e.g. a footer nav).
Menu triggers carry aria-haspopup and aria-expanded reflecting open state.
The current page link carries aria-current="page".
The open panel closes on Escape or an outside click, returning the page to its prior focus state.

variants.title: Navigation Menu
variants.description: A four-item nav bar with the Products mega-menu open (four described sub-links in a 2-column grid), plus plain Pricing and Docs links and a current-page About link.
accessibility: The mega-menu panel groups related links with short descriptions so users understand each destination before navigating.

variants.title: Navigation Menu (Dark)
variants.description: The same nav bar and mega-menu adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Active and current-page states remain visually distinct at dark-surface contrast.
